hints.content:
The fee that the first library charges for each book loaned is represented by the slope of the line of $C$. Since the formula for $C$ is in *slope-intercept form*, we can determine that the slope is $\green{1.5}$. This means that the first library charges $\$\green{1.50}$ for each book loaned.

The table of values for the second library shows that for each increase of $\blue{\text{books}}$ by $\blue{6}$, $\pink{\text{cost}}$ increases by $\$\pink{10.50}$. The fee that the library charges for each book loaned is the ratio of the corresponding differences in $\pink{\text{cost}}$ and $\blue{\text{books}}$:

$\dfrac{\Delta \pink{\text{cost}}}{\Delta \blue{\text{books}}}=\dfrac{10.5}{6}=\green{1.75}$

This means that the second library charges $\$\green{1.75}$ for each book loaned.

**Since $\green{1.5}<\green{1.75}$, the second library charges more for each book loaned.**

The subscription fee of the first library corresponds to the value of $C$ when $n=0$. To find it, all we need is to substitute $\blue n=\blue 0$ into the formula for $C$:

$\begin{align}
C&=10+1.5\blue n \\\\
&=10+1.5\cdot\blue 0 \\\\
&=\pink{10}
\end{align}$

This means that the subscription fee of the first library is $\$\pink{10}$.

We can extend the table of the second library according to the rate of change we found to find the value of $\pink{\text{cost}}$ when $\blue{\text{books}}$ is $\blue 0$:  

[[☃ image 1]]

This means that the subscription fee of the second library is $\$\pink{12}$.

**Since $\pink{10}<\pink{12}$, the first library has a cheaper subscription fee.**

question.content:
Antoine wants to get a subscription to a local library. There are two libraries, each of which charges a monthly subscription fee plus a fee for each book loaned.

The following equation gives the monthly cost (in dollars) of joining the first library as a function of the number of books loaned.

$C = 10+1.5n$

The monthly cost (in dollars) of the second library as a function of the number of books loaned is given by the following table of values:

$\text{Books}$ | $\text{Cost}$ (dollars)
:-: | :-:
$2$ | $15.50$
$8$ | $26$
$14$ | $36.50$

**Which library charges more for each book loaned?**

[[☃ radio 1]]

**Which library has a cheaper subscription fee?**

[[☃ radio 2]]

choices.content: They both charge the same for each book loaned
They both have the same subscription fee
